exact_matches: context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:115:| BISITE A.1 | The historical and adopted localizer axioms are different formulations. The literal Loc~(1) of XVI ms.~1 consists of isomorphisms, two-out-of-three, and the condition that $gf,fg\in W$ imply $f,g\in W$. Grothendieck calls the first two conditions \emph{saturation faible}, and all three \emph{saturation mod\'er\'ee}. Retract closure is added in Loc~(1 bis); strong saturation is Loc~(1 ter). The literal Loc~(3), XVI ms.~2, is absolute Theorem~A. Relative Theorem~A is Loc~(3 bis), ms.~3. In this paper, a fundamental localizer means the modern relative package specified in the conventions: weak saturation, the terminal-object axiom, and the assertion that a functor $u:A\to B$ over $C$ lies in $W$ whenever $u/c:A/c\to B/c$ lies in $W$ for every $c\in C$. Consequently no argument using relative Theorem~A is an argument from the literal absolute Loc~(3) alone. | claim (return: Proved) | XVI ms.1--3 |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:124:| BISITE A.10 | The three fibre axioms, with their quantifiers. For every $S\in\mathcal M$ let $\mathcal F_S$ be the full subcategory of $\mathcal M/S$ on the intrinsic fibrations. The three assertions at XII ms.~215--218 are \[ \begin{aligned} \mathrm{(a)}&\quad J_S:\mathcal F_S[(W_S^u)^{-1}] \longrightarrow(\mathcal M/S)[W_S^{-1}]\text{ is an equivalence};\\ \mathrm{(b)}&\quad W_S^u=W_S\text{ on }\mathcal F_S;\\ \mathrm{(c)}&\quad\mathcal F_S[W_S^{-1}]\longrightarrow \mathcal H[W_S^{-1}]\longrightarrow(\mathcal M/S)[W_S^{-1}] \text{ are equivalences} \end{aligned} \] for every full $\mathcal F_S\subseteq\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal M/S$. Axiom (a) implies equality of the strong saturations of $W_S^u$ and $W_S$ on $\mathcal F_S$. It does not by that argument imply equality of the original classes. Axioms (b) and (c) imply (a). | claim (return: Proved) | XII ms.215--218; XIIc B055--B065 |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:125:| BISITE A.11 | Enough intrinsic fibrations implies the exact fibrewise invariance. Suppose $\mathcal M$ has pullbacks, $W$ contains isomorphisms and satisfies two-out-of-three, and every map factors as a $W$-map followed by a member of $\operatorname{Fib}_W$. Then axiom (b) of A.10 holds, and \[ \operatorname{Fib}_W\cap W=W^u. \] No terminal object, accessibility, functorial factorization, or strong saturation is required for these conclusions. | claim (return: Proved) | XIII ms.10--11; XVI 4.4.1 |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:126:| BISITE A.12 | A functorial replacement proves every intermediate-subcategory comparison. Let $\mathcal A$ be a category with a class $W$ containing isomorphisms and satisfying two-out-of-three, let $\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal A$ be full, and suppose there is $R:\mathcal A\to\mathcal F$ with a natural transformation $\eta:1_{\mathcal A}\to iR$ whose components are in $W$. For every full $\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal A$, both inclusions induce equivalences \[ \mathcal F[W^{-1}]\longrightarrow\mathcal H[W^{-1}] \longrightarrow\mathcal A[W^{-1}]. \] In particular, such slice replacements into $\operatorname{Fib}_W S$, together with enough intrinsic fibrations, verify XII (a), (b), and (c). | claim (return: Proved) | XII ms.217--218; XIIc B060--B065 |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:127:| BISITE A.13 | The implication asked in audit row XIIc B062. The axioms (a) and (b) of A.10, even imposed at every base, do not imply (c). There is a counterexample with six objects, all finite limits and colimits, and strongly saturated $W$. It also refutes the analogous assertion for enhanced localizations. | claim (return: Refuted) | XII ms.207,217--218; XIIc B062 |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:128:| BISITE A.14 | The two fine axiom systems in XII ms.225--227. Suppose classes $L,P\subseteq\operatorname{Mor}\mathcal M$ contain isomorphisms and are closed under composition and pullback. Define $W_S^g=W_S^L$ and $W_S^d=W_S^P$. The clause called (a) on ms.~226, asserting preservation of $W^g$ by $L$-base change and of $W^d$ by $P$-base change, follows formally from the closure hypotheses. The clause called (b) on that page is the additional pair of assertions \[ \begin{aligned} (L/S)[(W_S^u)^{-1}]&\simeq(\mathcal M/S)[(W_S^d)^{-1}], &W_S^u=W_S^d\text{ on }L/S,\\ (P/S)[(W_S^u)^{-1}]&\simeq(\mathcal M/S)[(W_S^g)^{-1}], &W_S^u=W_S^g\text{ on }P/S. \end{aligned} \] Here $L/S$ and $P/S$ denote full subcategories on the corresponding structural maps. Under these additional equivalences, each fine theory is a contravariant pseudofunctor on all of $\mathcal M$. This conclusion does not require $L\cap P\subseteq\operatorname{Fib}_W$. | claim (return: Proved) | XII ms.225--227 |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:129:| BISITE A.15 | The four fibration classes and Loc (7), with reference localizer. For a fundamental localizer $W$, the four classes in XVI section~4 are distinct definitions. Besides intrinsic $\operatorname{Fib}_W$, one has Grothendieck fibrations; $\operatorname{Fib}^{\mathrm{weak}}_W$, tested by all arrows $T'\to T$ over the base with $T'$ and $T$ contractible in the category-homotopy sense; and $\operatorname{Parf}_W=\operatorname{Liss}_W\cap\operatorname{Prop}_W$. Here category-homotopy contractibility means that the identity functor is connected to a constant functor by a finite zigzag of natural transformations. It implies weak contractibility of the nerve, but replacing the test family by all weakly contractible nerves is a separate assertion, not the literal definition. Let $\mathcal G_W$ denote Grothendieck fibrations all of whose transport functors lie in $W$. For any arrow class $\mathcal F$, define \[ \begin{aligned} \mathrm A(\mathcal F)&:\quad\mathcal F\subseteq\operatorname{Fib}_W,\\ \mathrm B(\mathcal F)&:\quad W_S\cap\operatorname{Mor}(\mathcal F/S) \subseteq W_S^u\quad\hbox{for every }S,\\ \mathrm C(\mathcal F)&:\quad\mathcal F\cap W\subseteq W^u. \end{aligned} \] Loc~(7a), (7b), and (7c) are respectively $\mathrm A(\mathcal G_W)$, $\mathrm B(\mathcal G_W)$, and $\mathrm C(\mathcal G_W)$. For a reference localizer $V\subseteq W$, the conditions $\mathrm A_V,\mathrm B_V,\mathrm C_V$ replace $\mathcal G_W$ by $\mathcal G_V$. The condition $\mathrm D_V$ is $\mathrm A(\operatorname{Parf}_V)$, or its equivalent B and C forms once the hypotheses of A.17 are verified. Loc~(7F) is the factorization condition of A.11, not the inclusion of any one of these reference classes in $\operatorname{Fib}_W$. | claim (return: Proved) | XVI ms.27--41; POLES A.5--A.6 |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:130:| BISITE A.16 | The implications A to B to C and replacement transfer. Let $W$ and $\mathcal M$ satisfy A.11's initial assumptions. If every map factors as a $W$-map followed by a member of $\mathcal F$, then $\mathrm A(\mathcal F)$ implies $\mathrm B(\mathcal F)$. If identities lie in $\mathcal F$, then $\mathrm B(\mathcal F)$ implies $\mathrm C(\mathcal F)$. Suppose that each $p:X\to S$ in $\mathcal F$ admits a comparison $j_p:X\to R_p$ over $S$ in $W_S^u$, with $R_p\to S$ in $\mathcal G$. Then $\mathrm A(\mathcal G)\Rightarrow\mathrm A(\mathcal F)$ and $\mathrm C(\mathcal G)\Rightarrow\mathrm C(\mathcal F)$. If for every map $h:X\to Y$ over $S$ between $\mathcal F$-objects the chosen comparisons extend to a commutative square $R(h)j_X=j_Yh$, then also $\mathrm B(\mathcal G)\Rightarrow\mathrm B(\mathcal F)$. Functorial replacements suffice; the proof only needs these individual commuting squares. | claim (return: Proved) | XVI 4.4.1,4.4.9,4.4.10; POLES A.13--A.14 |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:131:| BISITE A.17 | The full Brown implication with all its premises. Suppose $\mathcal M$ has a terminal object and pullbacks, and $W$ contains isomorphisms and satisfies two-out-of-three. Let $\mathcal F$ contain isomorphisms and all terminal maps, be closed under composition and pullback, and admit a factorization of every arrow as a $W$-map followed by an $\mathcal F$-map. Then \[ \mathrm A(\mathcal F)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \mathrm B(\mathcal F)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \mathrm C(\mathcal F). \] This is the precise abstract assertion of XVI Lemma~4.4.3. The terminal-map premise is part of the statement, not a consequence of an arbitrary intrinsic-fibration factorization. | claim (return: Proved) | XVI 4.4.3; POLES A.13 |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:132:| BISITE A.18 | The weak constant-coefficient notion does not compose. The universal weak rational cohomological fibrations of I ms.~117--118 need not be closed under composition. The failure occurs for finite categories. Consequently that notion cannot be silently substituted for the intrinsic class in A.2 or for the class in Loc~(7F). | claim (return: Refuted) | I ms.117--118; GALOIS D.3 |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:133:| BISITE A.19 | The local-coefficient repair has an asymmetric conclusion. Let $\mathbb D$ be a derivator in presheaf variance. Suppose that for $p:E\to B$, after every strict base change, the right direct image of every constant coefficient is locally constant and its value at each base object is canonically the right Kan extension from the strict fibre. If $v:T'\to T$ over $B$ is fully faithful on locally constant $\mathbb D$-coefficients, then the pullback $w:E\times_BT'\to E\times_BT$ is a constant-coefficient $\mathbb D$-equivalence. This argument does not assert full faithfulness or an equivalence on all locally constant coefficients upstairs. If the same direct-image and base-change hypothesis is required for every locally constant coefficient on every base-changed total category, then the resulting cohomological-fibration class is closed under composition and pullback. The corresponding statements for left Kan extensions and homology follow by duality. | claim (return: Proved) | I ms.79--81,117--123; GALOIS D.2 |

context/companion/chunks/DER_XI-XIIa.tex:187:The displayed obstruction sequence should, however, be read as a provisional sketch. For a general nonabelian \(F\), the gerbe of lifts of a section \(\eta\) of \(R^1f_*F\) need not have the fixed band of \(f_*F\). Its band is obtained from automorphisms of local representatives of \(\eta\), hence involves inner forms of \(F\). For a direct check, take \(f:BC_2\to e\), constant \(F=S_3\), and the torsor represented by the inclusion of a transposition subgroup \(C_2\hookrightarrow S_3\). Its automorphism group is \(C_{S_3}(C_2)=C_2\), whereas \(f_*F=S_3\). The component of this torsor therefore cannot have the fixed band \(S_3\). Nor does nonabelian \(H^2\) behave as a group with a distinguished zero: neutrality is a condition on a gerbe. The notation \(G\) in the next paragraph is not defined. These are reasons to replace that portion of the argument, not reasons to reject the theorem. The classical framework is the theory of bands and gerbes in \citet[Chapter IV]{Giraud1971}; we give a direct repair that avoids choosing an obstruction class.

exact_matches: context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:116:| BISITE A.2 | Intrinsic fibrations and their unconditional closure properties. Let $\mathcal M$ have pullbacks and let $W$ be invariant under isomorphism of arrows. For $S\in\mathcal M$, let $W_S$ be the inverse image of $W$ under the source functor $\mathcal M/S\to\mathcal M$. Define \[ \operatorname{Fib}_W=\{p:E\to B\mid p^*: \mathcal M/B\to\mathcal M/E\text{ sends }W_B\text{ into }W_E\}. \] Thus every test is an arrow $v:T'\to T$ over $B$, with arbitrary structure map $T\to B$, and the tested arrow is $E\times_B T'\to E\times_B T$. This class contains isomorphisms and is closed under composition and arbitrary pullback. These assertions require no two-out-of-three axiom. If $W$ is closed under retracts, then so is $\operatorname{Fib}_W$. | claim (return: Proved) | XII ms.207--209; GALOIS D.1 |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:134:| BISITE A.20 | Properness does not imply local constancy of fibres. The inclusion $j:\{1\}\to[1]$ is proper in Grothendieck's presheaf convention, but its comma transition over $0\to1$ is $\varnothing\to e$. Thus the assertion about proper maps at I ms.~102, companion row Ib-C003, is false already for spaces and set coefficients. | claim (return: Refuted) | I ms.102; Ib-C003; GALOIS D.9; STRATA D.5 |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:135:| BISITE A.21 | Finite products and the one-fibrant-leg pullback comparison. Assume the hypotheses of A.11 and slice replacement equivalences as in A.12. In the localized fibrant slice over $S$, the product of $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ is represented by $X\times_S Y\to S$. Arbitrary derived reindexing preserves these finite products. Moreover, if $X\to S$ is intrinsic and $Y\to\overline Y\to S$ is a replacement with $Y\to\overline Y\in W$ and $\overline Y\to S$ intrinsic, then $X\times_S Y\to X\times_S\overline Y$ lies in $W$. Thus a strict pullback with one intrinsic leg computes the same relative homotopy object as replacing the other leg first. These are the formal assertions at XII ms.~241--248. | claim (return: Proved) | XII ms.241--248 |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:136:| BISITE A.22 | The intrinsic factorization content of the weak Quillen axioms. The conditions M2, M$'$, and M$''$ of XIII ms.~8 imply both intrinsic factorizations: every arrow factors as an intrinsic cofibration followed by a $W$-map, and as a $W$-map followed by an intrinsic fibration. They consequently imply the universal-equivalence equalities of XIII Corollary~1, ms.~10, and the fibrewise assertion of XIII Proposition~4, ms.~10--11. They do not identify the designated classes $TC,TF$ with $C\cap W,F\cap W$. | claim (return: Proved) | XIII ms.7--12,27--28; PATHS D.17 |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:137:| BISITE A.23 | The variance assertions of XIII section 4 are lifting adjunctions. Let $\mathcal M(I)=\operatorname{Fun}(I^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal M)$, suppose the ordinary Kan extensions used below exist, and let the two closed lifting pairs be $(C(I),TF(I))$ and $(TC(I),F(I))$, with $C(I),TC(I)$ defined objectwise. For $u:I'\to I$ one has \[ u^*C(I)\subseteq C(I'),\quad u^*TC(I)\subseteq TC(I'), \quad u_*F(I')\subseteq F(I),\quad u_*TF(I')\subseteq TF(I), \] and \[ \begin{split} u^*F(I)\subseteq F(I')&\Longleftrightarrow u_!TC(I')\subseteq TC(I),\\ u^*TF(I)\subseteq TF(I')&\Longleftrightarrow u_!C(I')\subseteq C(I). \end{split} \] If every component of $i\backslash I'$ has an initial object and the relevant coproducts exist, then all four containments in the last two equivalences hold. In particular injective fibrant diagrams are objectwise fibrant. For a walking-arrow diagram $X_0\leftarrow X_1$, injective fibrancy is equivalent to $X_0$ fibrant and $X_1\to X_0\in F$; this also implies that $X_1$ is fibrant. | claim (return: Proved) | XIII ms.45--50 |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:138:| BISITE A.24 | Ordinary Kan extensions do not automatically descend. For $(\mathrm{Cat},W_\infty)$, ordinary limits of finite diagrams need not preserve objectwise weak equivalences. Thus an ordinary $u_*$ in XIII ms.~45--50 cannot be identified with a derived $u_*$ without a derivability or fibrancy argument. | claim (return: Refuted) | XIII ms.45--50 |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:139:| BISITE A.25 | The noetherian sober Alexandrov qualification adds no infinite posets. If a poset with its Alexandrov topology is noetherian and sober, the poset is finite. Hence the apparently more general admissibility qualification in XIII ms.~60--61, requiring the Alexandrov space of $I^{\mathrm{op}}$ to be noetherian and sober, introduces no genuinely infinite poset beyond the finite case. | claim (return: Proved) | XIII ms.60--67 |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:140:| BISITE A.26 | The intrinsic finite floor does not provide all small Kan extensions. Finite limits, finite colimits, two-out-of-three, and both intrinsic factorization axioms do not imply existence of all small homotopy Kan extensions. A counterexample is the category of finite sets with isomorphisms as $W$. | claim (return: Refuted) | XIII ms.50--59; PATHS D.9 |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:141:| BISITE A.27 | Closedness upgrades historical exactness to both trivial-class equalities. Let $(C,TC,F,TF)$ satisfy the weak Quillen axioms of XIII ms.~27--28, including two-out-of-three for $W$, the two factorizations, and $TC\subseteq C\cap W$, $TF\subseteq F\cap W$. If both lifting pairs are closed and $W=TF\circ TC$, then \[ TC=C\cap W,\qquad TF=F\cap W. \] Moreover $W$ is retract-closed. With the finite limits and colimits of M0 these data are a closed model structure in the original finite-limit convention. The two intrinsic containments M$''$ make this structure proper. Thus a \emph{closed exact} structure, as required by the uniform hypothesis at XIII ms.~57, is stronger than the unqualified exact structure distinguished in A.22. | claim (return: Proved) | XIII ms.27--29,57 |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:142:| BISITE A.28 | The uniform theorem of XIII and the exact admissibility hypothesis. Assume exactly the uniform-left hypothesis of XIII ms.~57: for every $I$ in the specified diagram domain, the objectwise classes $C(I),TC(I)$ and their right orthogonals $TF(I),F(I)$ form a closed exact weak Quillen structure for the objectwise class $W(I)$. Let $u:I'\to I$ be a functor in the domain for which the ordinary presheaf right Kan extension $u_*$ exists. Then $u_*$ preserves weak equivalences between fibrant diagrams. It consequently induces a right adjoint \[ u^*: \mathcal M(I)[W(I)^{-1}] \rightleftarrows\ \mathcal M(I')[W(I')^{-1}]:\mathbf R u_*. \] If the comma categories $I'/i$ and their inclusions into $I'$ belong to the diagram domain, the canonical pointwise formula is \[ i^*\mathbf R u_*X\ \cong\ \mathbf R\!\lim_{(I'/i)^{\mathrm{op}}}X\|_{I'/i}. \] In particular every functor between finite posets is admissible under the source's hypotheses. No restriction to finite posets is necessary for admissibility once the relevant ordinary Kan extension and uniform diagram structures exist. In the historical numbering, this proves the right-hand Der~4 and Der~5 assertions of XIII ms.~61; these numbers do not mean modern Der~4 and strongness Der~5. | claim (return: Proved) | XIII ms.57--72 |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:143:| BISITE A.29 | The polarity calculation in II section 5 requires closure after a join. For any relation $R\subseteq P\times Q$, the maps $A\mapsto A^\perp=\{q\mid pRq\text{ for all }p\in A\}$ and its transpose define an antitone Galois connection on the power sets. Double orthogonality is an extensive idempotent closure; closed subsets are closed under arbitrary intersections, and their join is the closure of their union. If $P,Q$ are complete posets and the principal-polar condition (D$_0$) of II ms.~69 holds, write $c$ for the induced closure on $P$. For a subset $A\subseteq P$, its polar closure is the principal lower set \[ A^{\perp\perp}=\mathord\downarrow c\!\left(\bigvee A\right) =\mathord\downarrow c\!\left(\bigvee_{a\in A}c(a)\right). \] The final closure cannot be omitted from II formula~(5.20), ms.~76. One must also distinguish the element $c(\bigvee A)$ of $P$ from its principal lower set, a subset of $P$. | claim (return: Proved) | II section 5, ms.69--80, especially (5.20) |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:165:| BISITE B.17 | Intrinsic fibrations for truncation localizers. For $n\geq0$, a functor $p:T\to B$ lies in $\Fib_{W_n}$ if and only if, for every $X\to B$, the canonical map \[ \tau_{\leq n}B(T\times_BX)\longrightarrow \tau_{\leq n}BT\times_{\tau_{\leq n}BB}\tau_{\leq n}BX \] is an equivalence of $n$-types. The pullback on the right is a homotopy pullback in $\Spaces_{\leq n}$. For $n=0$ this is equivalent to the following elementary pair of conditions. context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:167:| BISITE B.19 | The full fence construction and its mapping-path factorization. Let $\mathcal P(C)$ be the category of all eventually constant diagrams $J\to C$ on the integer fence of B.8, with all natural transformations. Write $\sigma,\beta$ for the eventual left and right values. Then $(\sigma,\beta):\mathcal P(C)\to C\times C$ is smooth and proper for $W_\infty$, and therefore for every fundamental localizer. exact_matches: context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:183:| BISITE E.3 | A recognition theorem giving all three Kan functors. Suppose that the enhanced localizations $\mathscr E(S)=(\mathcal M/S)[(W_S^{\mathcal L})^{-1}]_\infty$ exist for bases $S$ in a category $\mathcal B$. Suppose we are given a functor $C:\mathcal B\to\Cat_\infty$ with small values and fully faithful functors $h_S:C(S)\to\mathscr E(S)$ satisfying the following precise presentation hypotheses. The category $\mathscr E(S)$ has all small colimits. Each functor $\Map(h_S(c),-):\mathscr E(S)\to\Spaces$ preserves all small colimits. These functors jointly detect equivalences. For each $f:S\to T$, postcomposition descends to a colimit-preserving functor $F_f:\mathscr E(S)\to\mathscr E(T)$ and there is a coherent equivalence $F_fh_S\simeq h_TC(f)$. Then the restricted Yoneda functors give equivalences \[ H_S:\mathscr E(S)\simeq\Fun(C(S)^{\op},\Spaces),\qquad H_S(X)(c)=\Map(h_S(c),X). \] Under these equivalences, $F_f$ is left Kan extension along $C(f)^{\op}$; it has right adjoint $f^*$, given by restriction, and this restriction has right adjoint $f_*$. These are coherent functors of the base, hence yield the requested pseudofunctors on homotopy categories. The locally constant subcategory has both adjoints to its inclusion. None of the presentation hypotheses is claimed to follow from E.1 or from factorization through intrinsic fibrations. | claim (return: Proved) | VI ms.108–113; XII ms.225–227 |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:195:| BISITE F.1 | The operations supplied by Der 1--4. Let $\D$ be a derivator on all $\mathbb U$-small categories, with presheaf variance, satisfying Der 1--4: coproducts of indexing categories give products, evaluations jointly detect isomorphisms, restriction has both Kan adjoints, and the pointwise comma formulas hold. Then every $f:X\to Y$ has \[ f_!\dashv f^*\dashv f_*:\D(X)\rightleftarrows\D(Y), \] where the display denotes the three functors with their usual alternating directions. For $A\in\D(X)$ and $y\in Y$ the formulas are \[ (f_!A)_y\cong\colim_{(y\backslash X)^{\op}} A, \qquad (f_*A)_y\cong\lim_{(X/y)^{\op}} A. \] The diagram under each limit is restriction along the forgetful functor to $X$, interpreted as a coherent diagram in the derivator. Comma squares are homotopy exact. Exact squares are closed under horizontal and vertical pasting, with the direction of their two-cell fixed. Strongness, pointedness and stability are not needed for these statements. | claim (return: Known) | I; VI ms.138–169 |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:204:| BISITE F.10 | A correspondence formalism on the smooth class, with an enhancement. Let $\mathcal V$ be a $\mathbb V$-presentable closed symmetric monoidal infinity-category whose tensor preserves $\mathbb U$-small colimits separately. Regard the ordinary category $\Cat_{\mathbb U}$ as an infinity-category by its nerve, so its pullbacks are the strict categorical pullbacks. Put $E=\Liss_{W_\infty}$. There is a lax symmetric monoidal functor \[ \Corr(N\Cat_{\mathbb U})_{E,\mathrm{all}} \longrightarrow\Cat_{\infty,\mathbb V},\qquad S\longmapsto\Fun(NS^{\op},\mathcal V), \] sending a span $X\xleftarrow{a}M\xrightarrow{b}Y$, $b\in E$, to $b_!a^*$. It is a pre-six-functor formalism in \citet[Definitions A.5.1 and A.5.6]{EFMann2022} and a six-functor formalism in Definition A.5.7 there. The restriction to homotopy categories is the indicated half of the represented derivator. This assertion uses the given infinity-category, not merely its valuewise homotopy categories. | claim (return: Proved) | Lead 3; Mann correspondence question |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:205:| BISITE F.11 | The terminology of the resulting operations. In F.10 every allowed map has $f^!=f^*$ and $f^!\one=\one$, compatibly with base change. Thus all these maps satisfy the cohomological smoothness formula with the trivial invertible twist; in the usual terminology for this identity they are cohomologically \emph{\'{e}tale}. This does not say that a Grothendieck-proper functor has $f_!=f_*$. Even a functor belonging to both Grothendieck classes need not have this ambidexterity. For a discrete bifibration with finite fibres, however, a stable coefficient category has the canonical ambidexterity $f_!\simeq f_*$. | claim (return: Proved) | Lead 3 terminology |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:206:| BISITE F.12 | The all-smooth class does not satisfy the later diagonal convention. The class $E=\Liss_{W_\infty}$ in F.10 is not closed under diagonals. Hence it is not a geometric setup under \citet[Definition 2.1.1 and Remark 2.1.2]{EFHeyerMann2024}, which add this requirement to the earlier convention. Restricting $E$ to discrete fibrations does satisfy the later convention and gives a six-functor formalism by the same construction. In that restriction the preceding cohomological \emph{\'{e}tale} description is unchanged. | claim (return: Refuted) | Mann versus later geometric-setup conventions |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:207:| BISITE F.13 | H\"ormann's diagram correspondences and the enhancement boundary. Fibered multiderivators encode the two halves and their exchange maps on the appropriate 2-multicategory of diagram correspondences. In \citet[Theorem 6.12]{EFHormann2017}, for pre-multiderivators $\mathbb E,\mathbb S$ satisfying Der 1--2, a strict morphism $\mathbb E\to\mathbb S$ is a left, respectively right, fibered multiderivator precisely when the induced map $\mathrm{Dia}^{\mathrm{cor}}(\mathbb E)\to\mathrm{Dia}^{\mathrm{cor}}(\mathbb S)$ is a 1-opfibration, respectively 1-fibration, of 2-multicategories. A closed monoidal derivator supplies the associated diagram-level six-operation structure. This does not turn all strict pullback squares of ordinary categories into exact squares and does not itself construct an infinity-categorical enhancement of an abstract derivator. | claim (return: Known) | Hörmann comparison |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:208:| BISITE F.14 | Comparison with relative smoothness and properness. For the indexed enhanced category $S\mapsto\Fun(NS^{\op},\Spaces)$ on the ordinary category $\Cat$ with strict pullbacks, the smooth and proper calibrations of \citet[Definition 2.3.1]{EFAnelWeinberger2025} are exactly $\Liss_{W_\infty}$ and $\Prop_{W_\infty}$ in our convention. This is a statement about that indexed category and that base category; replacing its base by $\Cat_\infty$ changes the pullback test. | claim (return: Proved) | Anel–Weinberger comparison |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:209:| BISITE F.15 | The genus-zero category and its geometric coefficients. For $n\geq3$, let $\Gamma_n$ be the pure orientation-preserving mapping class group of the $n$-punctured sphere. Let $\mathcal C_n$ have as objects the isotopy classes of essential multicurves, including the empty multicurve, and put \[ \Hom_{\mathcal C_n}(\sigma,\tau) =\{g\in\Gamma_n:g\sigma\supseteq\tau\}/\Delta_\sigma, \qquad [h]\circ[g]=[hg], \] where $\Delta_\sigma$ is generated by the Dehn twists in the curves of $\sigma$ and acts on the right. Set $T_{0,n}=\mathcal C_n^{\op}$. The exit category of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,n}(\mathbb C)$ with its dual-tree stratification is $N\mathcal C_n$. For every compactly generated presentable infinity-category $\mathcal V$, \[ \Shv_{\mathrm{cbl}}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,n}(\mathbb C);\mathcal V) \simeq\Fun(N\mathcal C_n,\mathcal V) =\Fun(NT_{0,n}^{\op},\mathcal V). \] Forgetting the last mark induces $Q:\mathcal C_{n+1}\to\mathcal C_n$, $\sigma\mapsto q\sigma$, $[g]\mapsto[\phi(g)]$, and $F=Q^{\op}:T_{0,n+1}\to T_{0,n}$. Here $q$ erases curves which become peripheral and identifies repeated isotopy classes, and $\phi:\Gamma_{n+1}\twoheadrightarrow\Gamma_n$ is the forgetful homomorphism. | claim (return: Known) | STRATA genus-zero comparison |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:210:| BISITE F.16 | Forgetting a mark is proper and need not be smooth. For every $n\geq3$, $F:T_{0,n+1}\to T_{0,n}$ is $W_\infty$-proper. context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:211:| BISITE F.17 | Geometric direct image and the boundary squares in this example. In the coefficient equivalence of F.15, the categorical right Kan functor $F_*$ is the ordinary topological direct image of constructible sheaves for $\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,n+1}(\mathbb C)\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,n}(\mathbb C)$. Categorical right base change agrees with topological proper base change for point fibres and for the squares obtained by a closed boundary inclusion. A boundary is represented by the replete full cosieve in the entrance category whose multicurves contain a curve with the specified label partition. The left Kan half supplies no universal smooth base-change statement for this forgetful functor. | claim (return: Proved) | STRATA geometric direct image and boundary base change |

context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:213:| BISITE F.19 | An exact proper class in the diagonally closed setup. context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:282:| RESIDUE I.4 | The preceding proof does not follow from \citet[Proposition A.5.10]{GHIJMann2022} by taking $I$ to be all smooth maps and $P$ to be the isomorphisms. exact_matches: context/DOSSIER_STATEMENTS_WITH_STATUS.md:222:| BISITE G.9 | The exact canonical equivalence criterion for finite posets. For a finite poset $P$ define the colimit-preserving transform \[ (V_PF)(s)= \lim_{t\in P^{\mathrm{op}}} \bigl(\Sigma^\infty_+\operatorname{Hom}_P(t,s)\otimes F(t)\bigr), \qquad V_P:\mathbb D(P)\longrightarrow\mathbb D(P^{\mathrm{op}}). \tag{G.9a} \] There is always a canonical formula \[ p_*^P\simeq p_!^{P^{\mathrm{op}}}V_P. \tag{G.9b} \] For spectra the transform (G.9a) is an equivalence if and only if each strict upper interval $P_{>p}$ is Gorenstein* over $\mathbb Z$. Here a finite poset $L$ is Gorenstein* when every open interval in $L$ with a newly adjoined bottom and top has the integral homology of a sphere; the empty interval is allowed as the $(-1)$-sphere. When this condition holds, (G.9a) gives an equivalence for every stable derivator, and it restricts to pointwise finite spectra or perfect complexes. This is a condition on this canonical transform; it is not a classification of every possible equivalence between the two diagram categories. | claim (return: Known) | Lead 4 corrected equivalence; Part G finite posets |
